L163@P4: 1. Overview of operating results, etc.
L164@P4: (1) Overview of operating results for the fiscal year under review
L165@P4: During the fiscal year ended May 20, 2026 (from May 21, 2025 to May 20, 2026), the Japanese economy
L166@P4: remained on a moderate recovery trend against a backdrop of improvements in employment and income
L167@P4: environment and an expansion of inbound demand. On the other hand, the prolonged Russia-Ukraine situation,
L168@P4: along with the escalating tensions in the Middle East centered around the U.S.-Iran relations, is casting a dark
L169@P4: shadow over the global economy due to increasing geopolitical risks. As a result, energy prices, including crude
L170@P4: oil, remain high, and raw material prices are rising against the backdrop of unstable exchange rates. Furthermore,
L171@P4: labor costs continue to soar due to labor shortages.
L172@P4: In Japan, prices continue to rise, and with stagnant real wage growth, consumers remain highly conscious of
L173@P4: protecting their livelihoods. This has led to an even stronger trend towards selective consumption and a
L174@P4: preference for lower prices in purchasing behavior, and the outlook for the economic environment remains
L175@P4: uncertain.
L176@P4: In the drugstore industry, the business environment surrounding the Company remains severe, particularly
L177@P4: noticeable intensifying competition due to reorganization through M&A and an increase in the number of stores,
L178@P4: and the shrinking of trade areas resulting from these factors.
L179@P4: In light of this environment, to create stores that are loved by the people of the local community, the Group has
L180@P4: worked to improve customer convenience and strengthen its expertise. In addition to improving the ratio of stores
L181@P4: with attached dispensing pharmacies, by further expanding the food category that includes fresh foods we are
L182@P4: accelerating conversion to a store format that allows for one-stop shopping in our “food & drug” business.
L183@P4: With regard to the establishment of new stores, we opened a total of 111 new drugstores to further promote our
L184@P4: establishment of a dominant presence: 26 in the Hokuriku and Shinetsu region, 17 in the Tohoku region, 20 in
L185@P4: the Kanto region, 11 in the Tokai region, 18 in the Kansai region and 19 in the Shikoku region. In addition, we
L186@P4: opened a total of 38 new dispensing pharmacies attached to drugstores: four in the Hokuriku and Shinetsu region,
L187@P4: four in the Tohoku region, 17 in the Kanto region (including one pharmacy attached to supermarket), five in the
L188@P4: Tokai region, seven in the Kansai region and one in the Shikoku region. Meanwhile, we closed eight drugstores
L189@P4: and nine attached dispensing pharmacies.
L190@P4: On June 2, 2025, the Company acquired all shares of supermarket operator Miwa Store Inc. (Kagawa Prefecture).
L191@P4: Additionally, on February 24, 2026, the Company acquired all shares of supermarket operators Tix Inc., Spot
L192@P4: Inc., Uoei Store Inc., Uosaito Inc., and Gakuyusha Ltd. (Niigata Prefecture). Spot Inc., Uoei Store Inc., and
L193@P4: Uosaito Inc. have been made consolidated subsidiaries, while Tix Inc. and Gakuyusha Ltd. are non-consolidated
L194@P4: subsidiaries. Furthermore, on February 24, 2026, the Company’s subsidiary, KUSURI NO AOKI Co., Ltd.,
L195@P4: received the transfer of the supermarket business operated by Cupid Co., Ltd. (Niigata Prefecture). With this, the
L196@P4: Company acquired 37 new supermarket stores.
L197@P4: As a result, the number of stores in the Group at the end of the fiscal year under review was 1,144, comprising
L198@P4: 1,107 drugstores (including 692 stores with attached dispensing pharmacies), six pharmacies specializing in
L199@P4: dispensing, and 31 supermarkets (including one store with attached dispensing pharmacy).
L200@P4: As a result of the above, the financial results for the fiscal year under review were as follows: net sales of 566,865
L201@P4: million yen (up 13.0% year on year), operating profit of 27,096 million yen (up 1.9% year on year), ordinary
L202@P4: profit of 27,722 million yen (up 0.8% year on year), and profit attributable to owners of parent of 17,133 million
L203@P4: yen (down 3.7% year on year).
L204@P4: Breaking down net sales by product category, heath product sales (pharmaceuticals and health foods, etc.) were
L205@P4: 46,367 million yen (8.2% of net sales; up 4.4% year on year), beauty product sales (counseling cosmetics and
L206@P4: face care products, etc.) were 64,412 million yen (11.4% of net sales; up 6.9% year on year), lifestyle product
L207@P4: sales (household products, etc.) were 94,726 million yen (16.7% of net sales; up 8.0% year on year), food sales
L208@P4: (food excluding fresh food) were 230,117 million yen (40.6% of net sales; up 16.0% year on year), fresh food
L209@P4: sales (fruit and vegetables, fresh meat, fresh fish and delicatessen items, etc.) were 71,409 million yen (12.6% of
L210@P4: net sales; up 21.4% year on year) and dispensing pharmacy sales (prescription pharmaceuticals prepared at
L211@P4-5: pharmacies) were 59,831 million yen (10.5% of net sales; up 15.3% year on year).- 3 -
L212@P5: (2) Overview of the financial position for the fiscal year under review
L213@P5: Total assets as of May 20, 2026 were 410,937 million yen, an increase of 58,472 million yen over those of May
L214@P5: 20, 2025. The main factors contributing to this increase were an increase of 20,044 million yen in buildings and
L215@P5: structures, net, an increase of 11,200 million yen in cash and deposits, and an increase of 6,967 million yen in
L216@P5: merchandise.
L217@P5: Total liabilities as of May 20, 2026 were 269,898 million yen, an increase of 63,193 million yen over those of
L218@P5: May 20, 2025. The main factors behind this increase were an increase of 41,584 million yen in long-term
L219@P5: borrowings, an increase of 7,728 million yen in notes and accounts payable - trade, and 6,976 million yen in
L220@P5: current portion of long-term borrowings.
L221@P5: Total net assets as of May 20, 2026 amounted to 141,038 million yen, a decrease of 4,721 million yen over those
L222@P5: of May 20, 2025.
L223@P5: The equity ratio as of May 20, 2026 was 34.3%.
L224@P5: (3) Overview of cash flows for the fiscal year under review
L225@P5: Cash and cash equivalents at the end of the fiscal year under review stood at 58,654 million yen (up 22.9% year
L226@P5: on year).
L227@P5: Cash flow positions and the factors affecting them during the fiscal year under review are as follows.
L228@P5: (Cash flows from operating activities)
L229@P5: Net cash provided by operating activities totaled 37,321 million yen (compared with 22,167 million yen provided
L230@P5: in the same period of the previous fiscal year).
L231@P5: This mainly resulted from profit before income taxes of 24,083 million yen, with the main inflow component
L232@P5: being a non-cash expense—depreciation of 14,472 million yen, and the outflow components including income
L233@P5: taxes paid of 9,011 million yen and an increase in inventories of 6,117 million yen.
L234@P5: (Cash flows from investing activities)
L235@P5: Net cash used in investing activities totaled 42,883 million yen (compared with 31,079 million yen used in the
L236@P5: same period of the previous fiscal year).
L237@P5: This mainly resulted from outflows of 33,480 million yen for purchases of property, plant and equipment due to
L238@P5: new store openings and so forth.
L239@P5: (Cash flows from financing activities)
L240@P5: Net cash provided by financing activities totaled 16,486 million yen (compared with 7,668 million yen provided
L241@P5: by the same period of the previous fiscal year).
L242@P5: This mainly resulted from inflows of proceeds from long-term borrowings of 66,050 million yen for use in
L243@P5: funding construction of buildings for new stores, and outflows of 21,262 million yen for repayments of longterm borrowings and 23,869 million yen for purchase of treasury shares.
L244@P5: (4) Future outlook
L245@P5: With regard to the outlook for the future, the consumption environment is expected to continue to have an
L246@P5: uncertain future, with factors including continued increasing tension in the international situation, high energy
L247@P5: prices, and ongoing inflation pressure.
L248@P5: In the drugstore industry, competition with other companies, including in other industries, is increasing with
L249@P5: respect to store openings, pricing, and competition for human resources. In addition, industry restructuring moves
L250@P5: such as management integration and capital alliances between major drugstore companies are expected to
L251@P5: accelerate, leading to a continued challenging business environment. In this environment, the Company will
L252@P5: continue to drive customer-oriented store development and sales floor creation, while working actively to
L253@P5: increase customer satisfaction through measures including employee training, promotion of low-cost operations,
L254@P5: and expansion of fresh food sales.
L255@P5: In the Company’s store investment plan for the fiscal year ending May 20, 2027, we plan to open 90 drug stores
L256@P5: as part of further strengthening our market dominance strategy. Our existing stores will continue reviewing
L257@P5: product lineups and working to increase the composition ratio of food products, with an emphasis on fresh foods,
L258@P5: and the Company will work to strengthen and expand its “food & drug” business. For dispensing pharmacies,
L259@P5: the Company plans to open 31 new drug stores with attached dispensing pharmacies to expand its business in the
L260@P5: dispensing pharmacy market. Looking ahead, the Company will work to increase the ratio of drug stores with
L261@P5-6: attached dispensing pharmacies serving as local community pharmacies.- 4 -
L262@P6: As a result of the above, the Company’s forecast for consolidated financial results for the fiscal year ending May
L263@P6: 20, 2027 is for net sales of 640.0 billion yen (up 12.9% year on year), operating profit of 32,000 million yen (up
L264@P6: 18.1% year on year), ordinary profit of 30,800 million yen (up 11.1% year on year), and profit attributable to
L265@P6: owners of parent of 19,000 million yen (up 10.9% year on year).
L266@P6: 2. Basic policy regarding selection of accounting standards
L267@P6: The Group applies the Japanese GAAP for accounting standards in order to ensure comparability among other
L268@P6: domestic companies in the same industry.
L269@P6: With respect to the adoption of International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS), the Group follows a policy
L270@P6-7: of responding in a suitable manner after giving consideration to various circumstances in Japan and overseas.- 5 -
